_note: Daily English for IT. Levels: foundation (everyday workplace words), professional (working in a team and with clients), expert (senior, architecture and leadership language). 'text' is what the learner says; 'aliases' are other accepted forms when they use the item in a sentence.

items.meaning: End of day: by the end of today's working day.
items.example: I will send the report by EOD.
items.prompt: Your manager asks when the bug fix will be ready. Answer using EOD.

items.meaning: Estimated time of arrival or completion: when something should be done.
items.example: The ETA for the release is Friday afternoon.
items.prompt: A client asks when the feature will be live. Give an ETA.

items.meaning: Looks good to me: approval after a code review.
items.example: Left two comments, but once they're fixed, LGTM.
items.prompt: A teammate asks you to review their pull request. Reply with your verdict using LGTM.

items.meaning: Pull request: a proposed code change waiting for review.
items.example: I've opened a PR for the caching change.
items.prompt: Ask a colleague to review your change, using PR.

items.meaning: Knowledge transfer: a session where one person passes on what they know.
items.example: Let's book a KT session before Priya goes on leave.
items.prompt: Explain why you want a knowledge transfer session before a colleague leaves. Use KT.

items.meaning: User acceptance testing: the client checks the work before sign-off.
items.example: The client signs off after UAT next week.
items.prompt: Tell your manager the client's testing is next week. Use UAT.

items.meaning: Service level agreement: the promised response or uptime targets.
items.example: Our SLA promises a reply within four hours.
items.prompt: A customer asks how fast you respond. Answer using SLA.

items.meaning: Root cause analysis: finding why something failed, not just fixing it.
items.example: We wrote an RCA after the outage.
items.prompt: Explain that you will write an RCA after the incident. Use RCA.

items.meaning: Too long, didn't read: a short summary at the top.
items.example: TL;DR: the migration is done and the tests pass.
items.prompt: Start a short update with a TL;DR about your project.

items.meaning: Out of office: you are not working that day.
items.example: I'll be OOO on Monday.
items.prompt: Reply to a meeting invite saying you are out of office on Monday. Use OOO.

items.meaning: Business as usual: the regular work, not a special project.
items.example: Support tickets are BAU for the team.
items.prompt: Say that answering support tickets is normal daily work. Use BAU.

items.meaning: Proof of concept: a small test that shows an idea can work.
items.example: We built a PoC before committing to the plan.
items.prompt: Explain that you built a small test first. Use PoC.

items.meaning: Minimum viable product: the smallest version that is still useful.
items.example: Let's ship the MVP first and add features later.
items.prompt: Suggest launching the smallest useful version first. Use MVP.

items.meaning: Application programming interface: how two programs talk to each other.
items.example: The payments API returns the status in JSON.
items.prompt: Explain to a non-technical manager what an API is. Use API.

items.meaning: Continuous integration and delivery: every change is built, tested and released automatically.
items.example: Every merge runs through our CI/CD pipeline.
items.prompt: Explain in one sentence what CI/CD means to a new team member.

items.meaning: Shortcuts in the code that make future work slower.
items.example: We'll schedule time to pay down tech debt.
items.prompt: Tell your manager why the team should fix some old code. Use tech debt.

items.meaning: A rare input or situation that the normal logic doesn't cover well.
items.example: Did you test the empty-cart edge case?
items.prompt: Ask a colleague whether they tested an unusual situation. Use edge case.

items.meaning: The conditions a feature must meet to be accepted as done.
items.example: The acceptance criteria are in the ticket.
items.prompt: Ask the product owner what the acceptance criteria are. Use acceptance criteria.

items.meaning: An urgent fix released straight to production.
items.example: We pushed a hotfix for the login bug.
items.prompt: Say you will release an urgent fix tonight. Use hotfix.

items.meaning: Returning to the previous working version after a bad release.
items.example: We rolled back the release within ten minutes.
items.prompt: Explain that you reverted the release. Use rollback.

items.meaning: A temporary way around a problem until the real fix is ready.
items.example: The workaround keeps checkout running until Friday.
items.prompt: Explain a temporary fix to a stakeholder. Use workaround.

items.meaning: Something your work needs before it can finish, such as another team or service.
items.example: We're blocked by a dependency on the payments team.
items.prompt: Say your task depends on another team's work. Use dependency.

items.meaning: A meeting to prepare upcoming tasks so the team can estimate them.
items.example: Backlog refinement is on Thursday.
items.prompt: Invite a colleague to the refinement meeting. Use backlog refinement.

items.meaning: A short team meeting to review what went well and what to improve.
items.example: Let's talk about it in the retro.
items.prompt: Suggest raising a problem in the sprint retro. Use retro.

items.meaning: A short daily team update on progress and blockers.
items.example: I'll mention it in stand-up tomorrow.
items.prompt: Say you'll raise the issue at the daily stand-up. Use stand-up.

items.meaning: Extra work added to a project without changing the plan or the time.
items.example: Those extra features are scope creep.
items.prompt: Politely say a new request is beyond the agreed work. Use scope creep.

items.meaning: Quick, easy improvements that give a good result for little effort.
items.example: Caching the lookup is low-hanging fruit.
items.prompt: Suggest an easy speed improvement to the team. Use low-hanging fruit.

items.meaning: A detailed look at one topic.
items.example: Let's do a deep dive on the outage.
items.prompt: Propose a detailed review of a problem. Use deep dive.

items.meaning: I'll return to this later, when I have the answer.
items.example: I'll circle back with the numbers tomorrow.
items.prompt: Someone asks a question you can't answer now. Reply using 'circle back'.

items.meaning: I can't continue until someone or something is ready.
items.example: I'm blocked on the test environment.
items.prompt: Tell your manager you can't continue without the test environment. Use 'blocked on'.

items.meaning: A polite way to ask for more detail.
items.example: Could you clarify what 'done' means here?
items.prompt: You didn't understand the requirement. Ask for clarification politely.

items.meaning: I'll confirm this before I say it is correct.
items.example: Let me double-check the figures before I send them.
items.prompt: Tell a client you will confirm the numbers before sending them. Use 'double-check'.

items.meaning: A short warning about something coming.
items.example: Heads-up, the deployment moves to six pm.
items.prompt: Warn your team that the release time changed. Start with 'Heads-up'.

items.meaning: Let's leave this topic for now and come back later.
items.example: Let's park it and discuss it after the release.
items.prompt: Suggest postponing a discussion that is off-topic. Use 'park it'.

items.meaning: The work is progressing as planned.
items.example: We're on track for the Friday release.
items.prompt: Give your manager a quick progress update. Use 'on track'.

items.meaning: I'll contact you again about this.
items.example: I'll follow up with the client on Monday.
items.prompt: Tell a colleague you will remind the client on Monday. Use 'follow up'.

items.meaning: Formal approval that the work is accepted.
items.example: We need sign-off from the product owner.
items.prompt: Ask the product owner to approve the work. Use 'sign-off'.

items.meaning: Point out a risk or problem so people notice it.
items.example: I'll flag this risk in the status report.
items.prompt: Tell your lead you will raise a risk in the report. Use 'flag'.

items.meaning: A friendly way to agree to a plan.
items.example: Sounds good, let's go with option two.
items.prompt: Agree politely to a suggested plan. Use 'sounds good'.

items.meaning: Work from home.
items.example: I'm WFH on Friday, but I'm online all day.
items.prompt: Tell your team you are working from home on Friday. Use WFH.

items.meaning: For your information: sharing something, no action needed.
items.example: FYI, the meeting room has moved to level two.
items.prompt: Send a colleague a note about a room change, using FYI.

items.meaning: As soon as possible.
items.example: Can you check the logs ASAP?
items.prompt: Ask a colleague to look at a bug quickly. Use ASAP.

items.meaning: To be decided or confirmed later.
items.example: The venue is TBD.
items.prompt: Tell your manager the venue is not decided yet. Use TBD.

items.meaning: I'll take care of it now.
items.example: Thanks for flagging that, I'm on it.
items.prompt: Reply to a colleague who asked you to fix a bug. Use 'I'm on it'.

items.meaning: Let's talk briefly to share updates.
items.example: Let's sync up after lunch about the release.
items.prompt: Suggest a short call with a teammate later today. Use 'sync up'.

items.meaning: The impact a change or failure could have if it goes wrong.
items.example: We limited the blast radius by rolling out to one region first.
items.prompt: Explain to your director why the rollout starts with one region. Use 'blast radius'.

items.meaning: A way for a slow part of a system to slow the parts that feed it.
items.example: Without backpressure, the queue grew until the service fell over.
items.prompt: Explain why the queue needs backpressure. Use 'backpressure'.

items.meaning: Doing an operation twice has the same effect as doing it once.
items.example: We made the payment endpoint idempotent so retries are safe.
items.prompt: A reviewer asks why retries are safe. Use 'idempotent'.

items.meaning: Copies of data catch up with each other after a short delay.
items.example: The read model uses eventual consistency, so counts can lag by seconds.
items.prompt: Explain to a product manager why a count can lag. Use 'eventual consistency'.

items.meaning: Gaining one good thing by accepting a cost somewhere else.
items.example: The trade-off is faster delivery against more maintenance later.
items.prompt: Present two options and the trade-off between them. Use 'trade-off'.

items.meaning: The one authoritative place where a piece of data is kept.
items.example: Finance is the single source of truth for invoices.
items.prompt: Say which system should own customer records. Use 'single source of truth'.

items.meaning: How much unreliability a service may have before work shifts to reliability.
items.example: We ran out of error budget, so we paused feature releases.
items.prompt: Explain why you are pausing releases this sprint. Use 'error budget'.

items.meaning: Service level objective: the internal reliability target.
items.example: Our SLO is 99.9 percent availability each month.
items.prompt: Explain the reliability target to a new product owner. Use SLO.

items.meaning: Repetitive manual operational work that could be automated.
items.example: Renewing certificates by hand was toil, so we automated it.
items.prompt: Argue for automating a weekly manual task. Use 'toil'.

items.meaning: A review of an incident that looks at causes and fixes, not at people.
items.example: We held a blameless postmortem and shared the actions.
items.prompt: Describe how you will review the outage without blaming anyone. Use 'blameless postmortem'.

items.meaning: Releasing to a small share of users first, to catch problems early.
items.example: The canary release went to five percent of traffic first.
items.prompt: Propose releasing a risky change gradually. Use 'canary release'.

items.meaning: A switch that turns a feature on or off without a new release.
items.example: We hid the new checkout behind a feature flag.
items.prompt: Explain how you would release unfinished code safely. Use 'feature flag'.

items.meaning: A pattern that stops calls to a failing service for a while.
items.example: A circuit breaker stops retries piling up on the failing service.
items.prompt: Explain how the app avoids hammering a failing dependency. Use 'circuit breaker'.

items.meaning: Understanding a system's health from its logs, metrics and traces.
items.example: Better observability halved our investigation time.
items.prompt: Ask for budget to improve monitoring. Use 'observability'.

items.meaning: A plan of the technical work for the coming quarters.
items.example: Platform stability is the first item on the technical roadmap.
items.prompt: Tell the leadership team what goes on the roadmap next. Use 'technical roadmap'.

items.meaning: Remove work from a plan to meet a date.
items.example: We had to descope the reporting module to hit the deadline.
items.prompt: Propose removing a feature to meet the date. Use 'descope'.

items.meaning: Reduce the chance that a plan fails.
items.example: We prototyped the integration to de-risk it.
items.prompt: Explain why you prototype before committing. Use 'de-risk'.

items.meaning: How many people could leave before a project is in trouble.
items.example: Only one engineer knows the billing code, so our bus factor is one.
items.prompt: Point out a knowledge risk in the team. Use 'bus factor'.

items.meaning: Respectfully disagree with, or refuse, a request, giving reasons.
items.example: I'd like to push back on the deadline, because testing needs two weeks.
items.prompt: Politely disagree with an unrealistic deadline. Use 'push back'.

items.meaning: A small, optional comment in a code review.
items.example: Nit: rename this variable for clarity.
items.prompt: Leave a small optional suggestion on a pull request. Use 'nit'.

items.meaning: The one goal every decision is measured against.
items.example: Customer retention is our north star this year.
items.prompt: Explain the goal the team should measure everything against. Use 'north star'.

items.meaning: Spending a lot of time on small, easy decisions while the big one waits.
items.example: We spent an hour on the logo colour, which is bikeshedding.
items.prompt: Tell the meeting you need to focus on the bigger decision. Use 'bikeshedding'.

items.meaning: The standard, supported way of doing something that teams are encouraged to use.
items.example: Teams use the paved road for deployments unless they have a reason not to.
items.prompt: Explain why teams should use the standard deployment path. Use 'paved road'.

items.meaning: Checks and limits that keep a process safe without blocking people.
items.example: We set guardrails on spending so teams can experiment safely.
items.prompt: Describe the checks you would put around AI tools in production. Use 'guardrails'.

items.meaning: Mark a feature as going away, with a date and a replacement.
items.example: We will deprecate the v1 API next year, with six months' notice.
items.prompt: Tell customers an old API is being retired. Use 'deprecate'.

items.meaning: Reduce the impact of a problem before it is fully fixed.
items.example: We mitigate the outage by failing over to the backup region, then fix the cause later.
items.prompt: Explain the temporary action you took during an outage. Use 'mitigate'.

items.meaning: Agreement among the people affected about direction and priorities.
items.example: Stakeholder alignment took three workshops before we started.
items.prompt: Explain how you will get product, legal and sales agreeing. Use 'stakeholder alignment'.

items.meaning: By the way: adding a side note.
items.example: BTW, the client prefers email over calls.
items.prompt: Say what 'BTW' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'BTW'.

items.meaning: Copy: include someone on an email so they can see it.
items.example: I've CC'd Ravi so he knows about the change.
items.prompt: Say what 'CC' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'CC'.

items.meaning: Thank you before the other person has done the task.
items.example: Thanks in advance for reviewing the document.
items.prompt: Say what 'thanks in advance' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'thanks in advance'.

items.meaning: A polite way to say you will assist.
items.example: Happy to help with the migration on Tuesday.
items.prompt: Say what 'happy to help' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'happy to help'.

items.meaning: It's fine, you don't need to apologise.
items.example: No worries, we can move the call to tomorrow.
items.prompt: Say what 'no worries' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'no worries'.

items.meaning: An apology for replying or delivering late.
items.example: Sorry for the delay, I was in a workshop all morning.
items.prompt: Say what 'sorry for the delay' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'sorry for the delay'.

items.meaning: Please tell me when you have an answer.
items.example: Let me know if the timing works for you.
items.prompt: Say what 'let me know' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'let me know'.

items.meaning: I'll reply later, once I have the information.
items.example: I'll get back to you once the logs are checked.
items.prompt: Say what 'I'll get back to you' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'I'll get back to you'.

items.meaning: A polite request for a document or detail.
items.example: Could you send me the latest version of the spec?
items.prompt: Say what 'could you send me' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'could you send me'.

items.meaning: A gentle follow-up on something you asked earlier.
items.example: Just checking in about the invoice from last week.
items.prompt: Say what 'just checking in' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'just checking in'.

items.meaning: You will arrive or reply later than planned.
items.example: I'm running late, so please start without me.
items.prompt: Say what 'running late' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'running late'.

items.meaning: Telling someone when you are available.
items.example: I'm free at three o'clock, if that suits you.
items.prompt: Say what 'I'm free at' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'I'm free at'.

items.meaning: A polite way to check someone can talk now.
items.example: Is this a good time to talk about the report?
items.prompt: Say what 'is this a good time' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'is this a good time'.

items.meaning: Move a meeting or task to a different time.
items.example: Can we reschedule the review to Thursday?
items.prompt: Say what 'reschedule' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'reschedule'.

items.meaning: Work in progress: something not finished yet.
items.example: The design is still WIP, so please don't share it.
items.prompt: Say what 'WIP' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'WIP'.

items.meaning: Questions and answers, or quality assurance testing.
items.example: We'll finish with a short Q&A session.
items.prompt: Say what 'Q&A' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'Q&A'.

items.meaning: The list of topics for a meeting.
items.example: Please add your point to the agenda before Monday.
items.prompt: Say what 'agenda' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'agenda'.

items.meaning: Tasks agreed in a meeting, with an owner.
items.example: Let's review the action items at the end of the call.
items.prompt: Say what 'action items' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'action items'.

items.meaning: The written record of what was said in a meeting.
items.example: I'll share the minutes after the call.
items.prompt: Say what 'minutes' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'minutes'.

items.meaning: The date or time by which something must be done.
items.example: The deadline for the report is Friday noon.
items.prompt: Say what 'deadline' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'deadline'.

items.meaning: A piece of work that is handed over at the end of a task.
items.example: The main deliverable is the test report.
items.prompt: Say what 'deliverable' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'deliverable'.

items.meaning: An important point in a project, often a checkpoint.
items.example: We reached the first milestone on time.
items.prompt: Say what 'milestone' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'milestone'.

items.meaning: What must be done before other things.
items.example: Login bugs are the top priority this week.
items.prompt: Say what 'priority' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'priority'.

items.meaning: A message to help someone remember something.
items.example: I've set a reminder for the client call.
items.prompt: Say what 'reminder' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'reminder'.

items.meaning: A short report on progress.
items.example: Here's a quick status update on the migration.
items.prompt: Say what 'status update' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'status update'.

items.meaning: A tracked request or task in a work system.
items.example: I've raised a ticket for the broken export.
items.prompt: Say what 'ticket' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'ticket'.

items.meaning: A mistake in software that makes it behave wrongly.
items.example: We found a bug in the discount logic.
items.prompt: Say what 'bug' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'bug'.

items.meaning: A version of software made available to users.
items.example: The next release goes out on Tuesday.
items.prompt: Say what 'release' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'release'.

items.meaning: Put new software live on a server.
items.example: We deploy to staging every morning.
items.prompt: Say what 'deploy' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'deploy'.

items.meaning: A test environment that is close to live.
items.example: Please test the feature on staging first.
items.prompt: Say what 'staging' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'staging'.

items.meaning: The live system that real users use.
items.example: The bug reached production last night.
items.prompt: Say what 'production' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'production'.

items.meaning: A copy of data kept in case the original is lost.
items.example: Make a backup before you change the database.
items.prompt: Say what 'backup' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'backup'.

items.meaning: The step where a user proves who they are to use a system.
items.example: The login page is loading slowly.
items.prompt: Say what 'login' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'login'.

items.meaning: An event where people gather to discuss something.
items.example: We have a meeting at ten about the release.
items.prompt: Say what 'meeting' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'meeting'.

items.meaning: A private meeting between two people, often a manager and a team member.
items.example: I have a one-on-one with my manager on Friday.
items.prompt: Say what 'one-on-one' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'one-on-one'.

items.meaning: Away from work for holiday or other reasons.
items.example: Priya is on leave until the twentieth.
items.prompt: Say what 'on leave' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'on leave'.

items.meaning: Passing your work and knowledge to someone else.
items.example: I'll prepare a handover before I go on leave.
items.prompt: Say what 'handover' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'handover'.

items.meaning: A short conversation to see how things are going.
items.example: Let's have a quick check-in at the end of the week.
items.prompt: Say what 'check-in' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'check-in'.

items.meaning: To access a system with your username and password.
items.example: I can't log in to the staging server.
items.prompt: Say what 'log in' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'log in'.

items.meaning: A problem that needs attention.
items.example: There's an issue with the payment page.
items.prompt: Say what 'issue' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'issue'.

items.meaning: Needing attention now, before anything else.
items.example: This is urgent, so please look at it today.
items.prompt: Say what 'urgent' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'urgent'.

items.meaning: Statement of work: the agreed scope, deliverables and timeline for a project.
items.example: The SOW has been signed, so the work can start.
items.prompt: Say what 'SOW' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'SOW'.

items.meaning: Request for proposal: a client's formal call for bids.
items.example: We're responding to the RFP by Monday.
items.prompt: Say what 'RFP' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'RFP'.

items.meaning: Subject matter expert: someone with deep knowledge in one area.
items.example: I'll bring in our SME for payments.
items.prompt: Say what 'SME' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'SME'.

items.meaning: Non-disclosure agreement: a promise to keep information confidential.
items.example: Please sign the NDA before we share the designs.
items.prompt: Say what 'NDA' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'NDA'.

items.meaning: Key performance indicator: a measure of how well something is going.
items.example: Our main KPI is the checkout conversion rate.
items.prompt: Say what 'KPI' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'KPI'.

items.meaning: Objectives and key results: a goal with measurable outcomes.
items.example: Our OKR this quarter is to halve the bug count.
items.prompt: Say what 'OKR' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'OKR'.

items.meaning: Return on investment: the gain compared with the cost.
items.example: The ROI on automation is clear within a year.
items.prompt: Say what 'ROI' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'ROI'.

items.meaning: Change request: a formal request to change the agreed scope.
items.example: That feature needs a CR and extra budget.
items.prompt: Say what 'CR' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'CR'.

items.meaning: Finished enough for someone else to check it.
items.example: The pull request is ready for review.
items.prompt: Say what 'ready for review' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'ready for review'.

items.meaning: Not included in the agreed work.
items.example: Mobile support is out of scope for this phase.
items.prompt: Say what 'out of scope' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'out of scope'.

items.meaning: Useful, but not required for the work to succeed.
items.example: Dark mode is nice to have, not essential.
items.prompt: Say what 'nice to have' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'nice to have'.

items.meaning: Required for the work to be accepted.
items.example: Export to PDF is a must have for the client.
items.prompt: Say what 'must have' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'must have'.

items.meaning: A rough estimate, not a precise figure.
items.example: Give me a ballpark for the cost by Friday.
items.prompt: Say what 'ballpark' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'ballpark'.

items.meaning: Pass a problem to someone with more authority or expertise.
items.example: I'll escalate the outage to the platform lead.
items.prompt: Say what 'escalate' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'escalate'.

items.meaning: Tell people about a possible problem before it happens.
items.example: I want to raise a risk about the vendor's timeline.
items.prompt: Say what 'raise a risk' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'raise a risk'.

items.meaning: Step-by-step instructions for handling a known operational task.
items.example: Check the runbook before restarting the queue.
items.prompt: Say what 'runbook' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'runbook'.

items.meaning: Being the person responsible for responding to production problems at a set time.
items.example: I'm on-call this weekend, so call me if the alerts fire.
items.prompt: Say what 'on-call' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'on-call'.

items.meaning: A bug where something that worked before is now broken.
items.example: The release caused a regression in the search page.
items.prompt: Say what 'regression' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'regression'.

items.meaning: A quick check that the main features work after a deployment.
items.example: We ran a smoke test after the deployment.
items.prompt: Say what 'smoke test' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'smoke test'.

items.meaning: A period when no new code changes are allowed before a release.
items.example: We start the code freeze on Wednesday.
items.prompt: Say what 'code freeze' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'code freeze'.

items.meaning: The moment a system starts being used by real users.
items.example: The go-live is set for the first of the month.
items.prompt: Say what 'go-live' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'go-live'.

items.meaning: The switch from the old system to the new one.
items.example: The cutover happens over the weekend.
items.prompt: Say what 'cutover' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'cutover'.

items.meaning: Moving data from one system to another.
items.example: The data migration took three weekends.
items.prompt: Say what 'data migration' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'data migration'.

items.meaning: An old system that is still in use and is hard to change.
items.example: We still depend on a legacy system for invoices.
items.prompt: Say what 'legacy system' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'legacy system'.

items.meaning: Connecting two systems so they work together.
items.example: The integration with the bank is almost done.
items.prompt: Say what 'integration' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'integration'.

items.meaning: Something provided by an outside company or library.
items.example: The login uses a third-party service.
items.prompt: Say what 'third-party' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'third-party'.

items.meaning: An outside company that supplies a product or service.
items.example: The vendor confirmed the new date.
items.prompt: Say what 'vendor' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'vendor'.

items.meaning: Helping a new person learn the team and the work.
items.example: Onboarding a new engineer takes about two weeks.
items.prompt: Say what 'onboarding' means to a colleague in one sentence. Use 'onboarding'.

items.meaning: Someone affected by or interested in the outcome of the work.
items.example: We should update the stakeholders on Friday.
